newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen B index up at noon on SEG gains.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index up at noon on SEG gains.

text.p: Shenzhen's hard currency B share index was up slightly at midday on Monday, fuelled by gains in television tube maker Shenzhen SEG, brokers said.
The index inched up 0.06 point or 0.04 percent to 130.92 on turnover of HK$22.8 million.
The domestic A share market advanced 2.64 points or 0.64 percent to 412.09 on turnover of 2.36 billion yuan.
"The B share index was mainly pushed up by gains of Shenzhen SEG," an analyst at J&A Securities (HK) said. "Some institutional investors seem to be buying the stock."
SEG surged HK$0.36 or 7.47 percent to HGK$5.18 on volume of 1.9 million shares, making it the most actively traded B share issue and the morning's best performer.
"There are signs of a heating up of the B share market," the J&A analyst said.

But most investors are still taking a wait-and-see attitude in the interim reporting season, an analyst at China Guotai Securities said. So far, only two out of the 49 Shenzhen-listed B share companies have released their 1997 interim results. They must do so by August 30.
Bengang Steel Plates was the second most active counter, gaining HK$0.03 to HK$2.10 on volume of 1.8 million shares. The rises in Bengang also helped push up the B share index, analysts said.

They have said institutions wanted to lift Bengang to pave the way for forthcoming B share listings. Bengang has held below its offer price of HK$2.38 per share since it listed 400 million B shares in Shenzhen early last month.
Hainan-based hotelier Dadonghai was the biggest A share gainer, advancing 0.55 yuan or 6.89 percent to 8.53 yuan.
But analysts said that despite the A share index gains, the market remained in a consolidation phase.
